<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. VII.|ACCORDING TO S. MARKE.|105}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=7|verse=8}}† For leauing the commaundement of God, you hold the traditions of men, the vvashings of cruses and cuppes: & many other things you doe like to these. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=9}}† And he said to thē, Wel do you frustrate the precept of God, that you may obserue your ovvne tradition. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=10}}† For Moyses said, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 20, 12.''}}* ''Honour thy father & thy mother''. and, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Leu. 20, 9.''}}* ''He that shal curse father or mother, dying let him dye''. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=11}}† But you say, If a man say to father or mother, ''Corban'' (vvhich is a {{sup|‖}} gift) vvhatsoeuer proceedeth from me, shal profit thee: {{verse|chapter=7|verse=12}}† and further you suffer him not to doe ought for his father or mother, {{verse|chapter=7|verse=13}}† defeating the vvord of God for your ovvne tradition vvhich you haue giuen forth. and many other things of this sort you doe.

{{verse|chapter=7|verse=14}}† And calling againe the multitude vnto him, he said to them, Heare me al you, and vnderstand. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=15}}† {{sup|‖}} Nothing is vvithout a man entring into him, that can defile him. but the things that proceede from a man those are they that make a man {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ See the first annotation vpō this chapter.}}∷ common. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=16}}† If any man haue eares to heare, let him heare. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=17}}† And vvhen he vvas entred into the house from the multitude, his Disciples asked him the parable. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=18}}† And he saith to them, So are you also vnskilful? Vnderstand you not that euery thing from vvithout, entring into a man, can not make him common: {{verse|chapter=7|verse=19}}† because it entreth not into his hart, but goeth into the belly, and is cast out into the priuy, purging al the meates? {{verse|chapter=7|verse=20}}† But he said that the things vvhich come forth from a man, they make a man common. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=21}}† For from vvithin out of the hart of men proceede euil cogitations, aduouteries, fornications, murders, {{verse|chapter=7|verse=22}}† theftes, auarices, vvickednesse, guile, impudicities, an euil eye, blasphemie, pride, folishnes. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=23}}† Al these euils proceede from vvithin, and make a man common.

{{verse|chapter=7|verse=24}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 15, 21.''}}* rising from thence he vvent into the coastes of Tyre and Sidon: and entring into a house, he vvould that no man should knovv, and he could not be hid. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=25}}† For a vvoman immediatly as she heard of him, vvhose daughter had an vncleane spirit, entred in, and fel dovvne at his feete. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=26}}† For the vvoman vvas a Gentile, a Syrophaenician borne. And she besought him that he vvould cast forth the diuel out of her daughter. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=27}}† Who said to her, Suffer first the children to be filled. for it is not good to take the childrens bread, and cast it to the dogges. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=28}}† But she ansvvered, and said to him, Yea lord. for the vvhelpes also eate vnder the table of the<noinclude>{{rh||O|crummes}}</noinclude>
